items.eventTitle: Middle East — Erratic White Object Over Water
items.title: Middle East — Erratic White Object Over Water
items.description: Navy Range Fouler debrief plus 2 min 17 sec infrared video. A "solid white object" flew through the field of view making "erratic [movements] above the water." Sensor cycled contrast filters and zoom levels but never achieved a tracking lock.

items.title: Southern US — Air Force Sighting (PR-45)

items.title: Iraq, May 2022 — 5 UAP Cross Screen (PR-19)

items.title: Iraq — "Probable SU-27/35" (PR-21)
items.description: 10-second IR video showing two areas of contrast moving together. Mission report describes them as a "probable SU-27/35" — Russian Federation aircraft. AARO inserts a comment confirming SU-27/35 designation.

items.title: Syria — North-South Track (PR-22)
items.description: 14-second dual IR/EO video, single UAP "moving from north to south," duration under one minute.

items.title: Iraq, Dec 2022 — West-to-East (PR-23)
items.description: 10-second IR video. "Possible UAP" flying west to east; observer did not pursue.

items.eventTitle: UAE, October 2023 — Two Long Tracks (PR-26, PR-27)
items.title: UAE, October 2023 — Two Long Tracks (PR-26, PR-27)
items.description: Two CENTCOM video releases tied to D23: 43 seconds and 4 minutes 57 seconds of IR footage tracking areas of contrast through extended sensor maneuvering. Among the longest video releases in the tranche.

items.title: Greece, Oct 2023 — Sea-Skimming "90° Turns" (PR-34, PR-35)
items.description: Two reports two days apart. PR-34: UAP "flying just above the surface of the ocean," making "multiple 90-degree turns at an estimated 80 mph." PR-35: UAP "flying straight above the ocean towards land." 2 min 57 sec IR video shows the sensor tracking through reticle locks, contrast filters, and zoom cycles before losing it against the background.

items.title: INDOPACOM 2023 — Three Co-Moving Objects
items.description: INDOPACOM submitted 1 min 59 sec of IR video showing three distinct areas of contrast that "appeared to maintain a fixed position and orientation relative to one another."

items.eventTitle: Greece, Jan 2024 — Diamond on SWIR ONLY (PR-28)
items.title: Greece, Jan 2024 — Diamond on SWIR ONLY (PR-28)
items.description: Striking technical case. Diamond-shaped UAP with a non-maneuvering probe at the bottom, traveling ~434 knots (499 mph) — visible ONLY through Short-Wave Infrared (SWIR), invisible to visible spectrum and standard IR. Operator switched modalities live during the 2-minute encounter and lost the object when leaving SWIR.

items.title: INDOPACOM 2024 — "Football-Shaped Body" (PR-46)
items.description: 9-second IR video. Football-shaped body with three radial projections — one vertical, two angled at 45 degrees from the major axis. The most morphologically distinctive object in Release 01.

items.title: UAE, June 2024 — Inverted Teardrop (PR-29)
items.description: NORTHCOM submission. 21 seconds of IR video showing an inverted-teardrop area of contrast with a vertically linear trailing mass. Observer noted possible reflection from object in water; operator estimated 24,000 ft, 163 knots.

items.title: Syria, Oct 2024 — "Halo Effect" Cluster (PR-31, 32, 33)
items.description: Same-day cluster of three FMV camera observations. Operator reported "misshapen and uneven ball of white light" with multiple "glares or light" from "unknown origin," and a "light/glare halo effect" at the top of the FMV feed.

items.title: Djibouti / Africa 2025 (PR-43)
items.description: AFRICOM submission. 2 seconds of IR footage showing a small, barely distinguishable area of contrast crossing the field of view. The video is looped for viewing purposes.

items.title: Department of the Army 2026 (PR-49)
items.description: 1 minute 49 seconds of IR video. Sensor tracks an initial area of interest, then disengages and pans to track TWO areas of contrast. The most recent UAP video in Release 01.

items.eventId: DOW-UAP-PR27, Unresolved UAP Report, United Arab Emirates, October 2023
items.eventTitle: Unresolved UAP Report, United Arab Emirates, October 2023
items.title: Unresolved UAP Report, United Arab Emirates, October 2023
items.description: The United States Central Command submitted a report of an unidentified anomalous phenomenon to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) consisting of four minutes and 57 seconds of video footage from an infrared (IR) sensor aboard a U.S. military platform in 2023. An accompanying mission report, DoW-UAP-D23, mentions a UAP was observed during the mission. Video Description: 00:00-01:55: No content. 01:56: An area of contrast becomes distinguishable against the background in the center of the right side of the display. 02:04: The IR sensor pans to center on the area of contrast. 02:14: The sensor field-of-view narrows to zoom in on the area of contrast. 02:15-03:26: The area of contrast remains generally in the center of the sensor field-of-view. 03:27-04:57: The sensor motion causes the area of contrast to move erratically across the display. Due to this motion, the sensor system repeatedly loses and reacquires the area of contrast within the center area of the display. This video description is provided for informational purposes only. Readers should not interpret any part of this description as reflecting an analytical judgment, investigative conclusion, or factual determination regarding the described event’s validity, nature, or significance.

items.eventId: DOW-UAP-PR32, Unresolved UAP Report, Syria, October 2024
items.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Syria, October 2024
items.description: The United States Central Command submitted a report of an unidentified anomalous phenomenon (UAP) to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) consisting of six seconds of video footage from a full-motion video (FMV) camera aboard a U.S. military platform in 2024. An accompanying mission report, DoW-UAP-D32, described the UAP as consisting of a “misshapen and uneven ball of white light,” and reported that a “light/glare halo effect” occurred at the top of the FMV feed. Video Description: 00:02-00:04: An area of irregular color and brightness, mainly consisting of white and red highlights, appears near the center of the top edge of the sensor display. The area extends to a width of approximately one-third of the horizontal frame, with a vertical area comprising approximately one-sixth of the viewing area. Overall, its shape is best described as a horizontally-oriented half-oval bisected along its major axis. This video description is provided for informational purposes only. Readers should not interpret any part of this description as reflecting an analytical judgment, investigative conclusion, or factual determination regarding the described event’s validity, nature, or significance.

items.title: Unresolved UAP Report, Arabian Gulf, 2020
items.description: The United States Central Command submitted a report of an unidentified anomalous phenomenon to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) consisting of one minute and three seconds of video footage from an infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform in 2020. The original reporter digitally altered the imagery by pausing the video playback and adding a white line encircling an area of interest at timestamp 00:10, annotated with the phrase “U/I SMALL THERMAL SIGNATURE.” AARO did not edit the originally reported material, and this media is presented as received. Video Description: 00:00-00:09: An area of contrast brightens within the sensor field-of-view, becoming increasingly distinct against the background. 00:10-00:14: Playback pauses to display a white line encircling an area of interest, annotated with the phrase “U/I SMALL THERMAL SIGNATURE.” 00:15-01:03: Playback resumes, with the sensor panning to track the area of contrast against the background, generally maintaining the area of contrast’s position within the top third of the display area. During this period, the sensor cycles through several contrast and zoom settings. This video description is provided for informational purposes only. Readers should not interpret any part of this description as reflecting an analytical judgment, investigative conclusion, or factual determination regarding the described event’s validity, nature, or significance.
